criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml OLY-R6-02 has a mechanism naming exploration.rs and its result-recording function (not "none"), keeps owner "Athena", and has a measure ending `status: not shown` that names the exploration test via `cargo test -p athena-core exploration`.
criteria.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 -- docs/spec.toml` shows the mechanism changed from "none" to "crates/athena-core/src/exploration.rs: record_result stores an ExperimentResult ...". The owner is still "Athena". The measure names "cargo test -p athena-core exploration" and ends "; status: not shown". The diff touches only OLY-R6-02.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/exploration.rs defines a result type with exactly the variants Supported, Unsupported and Inconclusive and a function that stores one on an Experiment (Grep shows both).
criteria.evidence: I read exploration.rs. Lines 35-42 define `pub enum ExperimentResult { Supported, Unsupported, Inconclusive }`. Lines 85-92 define `pub fn record_result(e: &mut Experiment, result: ExperimentResult) -> Result<(), Refusal>`, which validates the experiment, refuses `Outcome::Pending` with `Refusal::NotConcluded`, and otherwise sets `e.result = Some(result)`.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core exploration`: new tests show a concluded experiment records each of the three results and reads them back, and an invalid (e.g. unbounded) or not-yet-concluded experiment refuses a result with a Refusal. The tests fail to compile or fail if the recording function is removed.
criteria.evidence: 7 tests passed. They include the new exploration_records_each_result_on_concluded_experiment, which loops over all three variants, asserts Ok, and reads back Some(r). They also include exploration_refuses_result_when_unconcluded_or_invalid: a Pending experiment gets Err(NotConcluded), and a Completed experiment with bound 0 gets Err(Unbounded); in both cases the result stays None. Both tests call `record_result` directly, so removing the function stops them compiling. I judged this from the code and did not remove it, because this role changes nothing.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` (including the xtask spec test): all pass, with no other spec.toml requirement changed.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks, reused from CI run 42932233342 for 32644da43c02, show fmt, clippy and test all passed. I also ran the xtask spec test myself: 30 passed, including the_real_spec_passes and every_active_requirement_has_a_mechanism_an_owner_and_a_measure. The spec.toml diff changes only OLY-R6-02.

findings.summary: record_result silently overwrites a result that was already recorded, and the pub `result` field lets callers skip the guard.
findings.evidence: record_result sets `e.result = Some(result)` without checking whether a result is already there. `Experiment.result` is `pub`, so code can set it directly without calling record_result. This matches how the existing `outcome` field works, and nothing outside exploration.rs constructs an Experiment, so it does no harm today. If results are later persisted or audited, consider refusing a second result or making the field private behind an accessor.

summary: The change does what the request asks. exploration.rs gains an ExperimentResult enum with exactly three values (Supported, Unsupported, Inconclusive), a `result` field on Experiment, and a `record_result` function. The function refuses an invalid experiment and one that has not concluded, and otherwise stores the result. Two new unit tests cover recording and reading back each value and both refusals. Both call record_result, so they would not compile without it. In docs/spec.toml, OLY-R6-02 now names this mechanism, keeps owner Athena, and has a measure that names `cargo test -p athena-core exploration` and ends `status: not shown`. No other requirement changed. I ran the exploration tests (7 passed) and the xtask spec test (30 passed). Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks from CI all passed. Every changed file is on the expected deliverables list. The only finding is minor: a recorded result can be overwritten, and the pub field can be set without going through the function.
